Can Sonnet improve

How the improvement loop works

A model proposes a change. Fresh runs decide whether it stays.

→→→→
Next round: use the retained version and the new evidence
Step 1 / Analyst

Start with what is actually known.

In the first round, Sonnet reads only the tasks’ public instructions. Later rounds add this experiment’s scores and execution traces, including unsuccessful candidates. Earlier experiments are excluded.

What can change?

The harness is the guidance and support around the model: instructions, skills, helper tools and supported hooks. Sonnet writes changes to this layer.

What stays fixed?

Sonnet 5.5, the native Claude Code conversation and tool loop, the chemistry tasks, their experimental budgets, and the official scoring rules.

What makes it recursive?

An accepted change becomes the starting point for the next proposal. Every tested change leaves evidence for the next round, even when it is discarded.

The keep rule

The first accepted candidate needs at least 3 passes out of 6. After that, a new candidate must beat the retained version’s total and lose no passes on either task. A tie keeps the previous version. Incomplete or errored evaluations block selection.

03

Follow the changes, round by round

The proposal, the check, the result, and the exact edit.

One model. Two different jobs.

Sonnet acts as the scientist when it runs a task, and as the editor when it revises the workflow. A separate Sonnet critic checks each proposal before testing. None of these roles changes the model’s weights.

This experiment takes inspiration from Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement. It uses its own five-round selection protocol and does not reproduce the paper’s full method or held-out evaluation.
